post_topic: The unglamorous production work that separates a live product from a demo that looks live
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title at top center in bold navy text: 'Demo That Looks Live vs. Actually Live'

Two vertical columns side by side, separated by a thin vertical divider line.

Left column header: 'Demo That Looks Live' — header text in amber #F5A623, with a subtle dashed border around the column.
Left column contains four rows, each with a red X icon followed by plain text:
— 'No analytics wired in'
— 'Blank browser tab (no favicon)'
— 'Broken social preview (missing OG image/metadata)'
— 'No signup attribution'

Right column header: 'Actually Live' — header text in blue #5a96ff, with a solid border around the column.
Right column contains four rows, each with a green checkmark icon followed by plain text:
— 'Real analytics capturing user behavior'
— 'Branded favicon in every browser tab'
— 'OG metadata rendering correctly on share'
— 'First-touch attribution captured at signup'

Below both columns, centered, a single amber #F5A623 callout box with text: 'None of this is a feature. All of it is the difference.'

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text 'Kelvin Davis' bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
